title: Payer Relations Memo: A New Primary Coverage During a PAP Therapy Equipment Rental
content:
# A New Primary Coverage During a PAP Therapy Equipment Rental

**Memo.** When a different primary coverage starts paying during a PAP Therapy Equipment rental — for example a move from a Medicare Advantage plan to Original Medicare Part B, or from commercial coverage to Medicare — a new rental period begins under the new coverage on the first date of service it covers, and the months paid under the earlier coverage do not count toward the new coverage's cap.

**Requalification.** Where the class requires the qualifying test on file and a new visit, the new coverage pays only once the qualifying test on file predates the new coverage and a new practitioner visit documents continued use and benefit; months before that visit are not billed to the new coverage.

**Verification.** The rental moves to the new coverage only once it is verified: the new coverage record is in status active, as the system's coverage records show.

**Owned devices.** A patient-owned device is not affected by a change of coverage.

## Effects of the move

| Item | Under the new primary coverage |
|---|---|
| Rental period | a new period begins on the first date of service the new coverage covers |
| Months paid under the earlier coverage | do not count toward the new coverage's cap |
| Months before the new practitioner visit (classes requiring it) | not billed to the new coverage |
| Patient-owned device | not affected |

**Example (hypothetical dates).** An Auto-Adjusting CPAP System (E0601) has 7 months paid under a Medicare Advantage plan. Original Medicare Part B becomes primary with a first covered date of 1 August, and its coverage record is active. A new rental period begins on 1 August with no months counted toward the new cap. The qualifying test on file is dated before 1 August, and the new practitioner visit takes place on 20 August; the months before 20 August are not billed to the new coverage.
